The CHK-014 stimulus requires the model to be off: contract.json:560 "Metastability model off, i_empty_thr=0, i_full_thr=8". The metastability model is defined per bit: spec:181 REQ-VER-001 "every bit of a synchronizer is modelled independently ... a random latency, chosen independently for each bit and each change". Other parts of the spec say the destination only sees valid Gray values: spec:477 "An invalid Gray value cannot occur in the model with one-bit changes", spec:684-685 "a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value ... the model is there to check that the FIFO flags stay pessimistic", and spec:1491 DEC-023 "the destination sees only valid Gray values at any frequency".
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:120 computes `w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s` (4-bit, modulo 16). Line 126 gives `o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (i_full_thr=='0) : (w_occ >= i_full_thr)` and line 106 gives full only when `reg_wgray == w_rgray_s ^ 2'b11<<..`. When the FIFO is not blocked, o_full_thr=1 together with o_full=0 needs w_occ in 9..15. That cannot happen if w_rgray_s is a value the read pointer really had. The sim branch of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 picks a 0/1/2 extra delay for each bit on its own (lines 158-169), and line 182 drives `o_q = sim_en ? sim_cur : ...`. In this run the read clock is fast (14/6 ns, base.s1.log:47) and the read Gray pointer changes about twice per write cycle. So a later bit change can show up before an earlier one. Example: 0000→0001→0011 with bit0 delayed by 2 and bit1 delayed by 0 gives w_rgray_s=0010 (binary 3) while the real pointer is 2. Then w_occ=2-3=15 and o_full_thr=1 while o_full=0. This mechanism is inferred; no waveform is available. The SVA a_CHK_013 (nnc_chk_wr.sv:123-127) also fires at the DUT ports (base.s1.log:239 "NNC_FAIL CHK-013 @1681000"), so this is not a cocotb sampling artifact.
analyses.test_does: Env(dut, per, ft=DEPTH, et=0) (test_async_gray_fifo.py:857). Ten times it writes one word, fills to 8, reads one word, then calls drain() (lines 865-897). The checker _on_w at lines 205-207 computes `exp = int(full == 1 and sw == 1 and busy == 0)` from the values sampled at the same edge and asserts `fth == exp`. At 1680691 ps it saw o_full=0, sw=1, busy=0, so exp=0, but o_full_thr=1. The test runs with MSYNC_EN=1 (base.s1.log:47), logs NNC_NOT_VERIFIABLE for exact latency (line 48) and keeps going (test lines 862-863). The contract asked for the model to be off.

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL model follows REQ-VER-001 word for word (spec:181, spec:653 "Each bit of the synchronized vector is independent"; cell_sync.sv:158-169). Independent 0..2 cycle delays per bit can reorder two Gray bit changes that are less than 2 destination cycles apart, which gives a vector value the source never had. That contradicts spec:477, spec:684-685, DEC-023 (spec:1491) and TEST-008 "flags never optimistic" (spec:1246). All 12 runs have the model on (e.g. base.s1.log:37 +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=1), and the failures cluster in dense or fast-source traffic. CHK-015, which uses isolated changes only, passes (base.s1.log:64-65), as expected if reordering needs back-to-back changes.
candidates.evidence_against: No control run has the model off or VLSIT_SYNTHESIS defined (grep for exact=True/SYN=True/MSYNC_EN=0 in sim_runs/ gives 0 matches), so the mechanism is not proven by a counter-experiment. No waveform shows w_rgray_s holding an illegal value.

candidates.evidence_for: Both the model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv) and the FIFO are RTL deliverables. Seen from the ports, o_full_thr=1 with o_full=0 at i_full_thr=8 breaks REQ-FUNC-010 in the shipped simulation branch. A model that keeps the vector coherent (one bit in flight at a time, as DEC-023 assumes for silicon) would remove the symptom.
candidates.evidence_against: The threshold logic itself (wr.sv:120,126) is exactly what REQ-FUNC-010 describes, and it gives w_occ<=8 whenever w_rgray_s is a legal past value. The model does what REQ-VER-001 literally asks.

analyses.failure: test_regression_random — CHK-003: i_empty_thr>=depth expected o_empty_thr=1 got 0 at 121854587 ps (12 of 12 runs)
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:287 CHK-003(b): "If i_empty_thr >= PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_empty_thr=1." REQ-FUNC-010 at rules.json:686. analyses.rtl_does: With et=8 (base.s1.log:192), o_empty_thr=0 needs w_occ=w_wbin_s-reg_rbin >= 9 (rd.sv:112,118), which needs w_wbin_s to be ahead of the real write pointer. This happens 237 ns into the test (base.s1.log:191-193), during the first "fill" phase (wd=1.0: writes every 10 ns against reads every 13.7 ns, test lines 524-530). The write Gray pointer then changes every source cycle, and independent per-bit delays (cell_sync.sv:158-169) can make the synchronized value show, e.g., 0010 (binary 3) while the source is at 0011 (binary 2). Filled to 8, that gives an estimate of 9. The SVA also fires (base.s1.log:245 "NNC_FAIL CHK-003 @121855000"). base.s4.log:174 shows the same effect from the other side: "CHK-032: occupancy 2 <= i_empty_thr 2 expected o_empty_thr=1 (never optimistic) got 0", i.e. a read-domain estimate above the true occupancy.

analyses.failure: assertion CHK-003 — o_empty_thr consistency for every 4-bit i_empty_thr (21 fails / 188920 hits, first at 57094000)

Model: spec:181 and spec:653 (each bit independent) vs spec:477 "An invalid Gray value cannot occur".
analyses.rtl_does: rd.sv:118 `o_empty_thr = w_rd_blk ? 1'b1 : (w_occ <= i_empty_thr)` with rd.sv:112 `w_occ = w_wbin_s - reg_rbin`, 4-bit modulo. For a legal w_wgray_s, w_occ is in 0..8, so (b) always holds. Every logged failure is the (b) form (for example base.s1.log:240,241,245; base.s3.log:157), which means w_occ > i_empty_thr >= 8: the estimate is out of range. w_wgray_s comes from u_sync_wr_gray (rd.sv:206-215), built from per-bit m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync instances whose sim model picks a 0..2 cycle extra delay for each bit and each change (cell_sync.sv:158-169, 182). That can reorder Gray bit changes that are less than 2 destination cycles apart. All runs have the model enabled (e.g. base.s1.log:229-238 "AFIFO_MSYNC ... enable=1").
analyses.test_does: SVA nnc_chk_rd.sv:58-62 checks (a), (b) and (c) at every posedge i_clk_rd with no disable (contract: "and while i_rst_n_rd=0"). The cocotb mirror is at test lines 243-249. The failures are rare (21/188920) and appear in dense or fast-source traffic, which fits random reordering. Isolated-change tests (CHK-015) pass.

analyses.spec_says: contract.json:524: "(a) if i_full_thr==0, then o_full_thr=1; (b) if i_full_thr > PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH (9..15), then o_full_thr=0; (c) if i_full_thr==PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_full_thr == (o_full AND i_rst_n_sw AND NOT o_sw_rst_busy); (d) ...". Model: spec:181 REQ-VER-001 per-bit independent latency, against spec:477 and DEC-023 (spec:1491).
analyses.rtl_does: wr.sv:120 `w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s` (4-bit) and wr.sv:126 `o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (i_full_thr=='0) : (w_occ >= i_full_thr)`. wr.sv:106 sets full only when w_occ is exactly 8 (MSB-inverted Gray match). Failures of type (c) (o_full_thr=1, o_full=0 at threshold 8) and (b) (o_full_thr=1 at threshold 9 or 12, base.s4.log:41,136) both need w_occ in 9..15. That cannot happen if w_rgray_s is a legal past read pointer, because the RTL never writes past full. w_rgray_s comes from per-bit cell_sync models (wr.sv:233-242; cell_sync.sv:158-169), which can reorder bit changes when the read clock is fast or reads are back to back (e.g. 14/6 ns in CHK-014, 23/10 ns in CHK-029). The model is enabled in every run.
